finding.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` is applied to ALL ranges, not just unbounded ones — an unrequested global semantics change to bounded-range aggregation, documented only inside the new "Whole-column / whole-row" section of the design doc
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }`. The issue only asks that unbounded ranges treat unused cells as contributing nothing; this changes how every existing bounded range (`=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` with blanks, `=COUNT`, `=MIN/MAX`, and any argument-position-sensitive function) is evaluated. docs/design/sheets/formula.md records the new rule as a note under the unbounded-range section ("Blank cells inside a range contribute nothing to aggregations (`Arguments.iterate` skips them)") rather than as a change to the canonical evaluation/arguments semantics, so the doc understates the blast radius of the behavior change.
